findings.explanation: This module creates google_secret_manager_secret.secrets, google_secret_manager_secret_version.this, google_kms_crypto_key.secrets, and google_project_service_identity.secretmanager, but declares zero outputs (no outputs.tf, no output blocks anywhere, confirmed by README's own 'No outputs' line). A caller who needs to grant further IAM access to the created secret (google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member), reference the KMS key elsewhere, or read back a secret version ID has no way to do so short of duplicating resource creation outside the module — defeating the point of using it as a module.
findings.remediation: Add outputs.tf exposing at minimum: secret_ids (map of name -> google_secret_manager_secret.secrets[*].id), secret_version_ids, kms_key_id (google_kms_crypto_key.secrets.id), and service_account_email (google_project_service_identity.secretmanager.email).
findings.title: Module exposes no outputs — callers can't reference the secret, KMS key, or service identity it creates

findings.explanation: rotation_period is hardcoded to "7776000s" (90 days) directly in the resource block. This is a different setting from var.rotation_period (which controls the secret's own rotation notification schedule, not the KMS key's rotation) — there is currently no way for a caller to choose a different KMS key rotation cadence (e.g. 30 days for stricter compliance requirements) without forking the module.
findings.fix:
In variables.tf, add:

variable "kms_rotation_period" {
  type        = string
  description = "Rotation period for the KMS crypto key protecting the secrets, in seconds duration format"
  default     = "7776000s"
}

In google_kms_crypto_key.tf, change line 5 to:

  rotation_period = var.kms_rotation_period
findings.remediation: Expose a variable (e.g. kms_rotation_period) with a default of "7776000s" and reference it instead of the literal.
findings.title: KMS crypto key rotation_period is hardcoded, not parameterized

findings.explanation: locals.tf reads secret.name and secret.secret_data off every element of var.secrets, but the variable's type only requires "a non-empty map of string attributes" — a caller passing [{ foo = "bar" }] satisfies the validation condition (length(keys(s)) > 0) but fails at plan/apply time with an unhelpful 'attribute name not found' error instead of a clear validation message naming the missing key.
findings.remediation: Type var.secrets as list(object({ name = string, secret_data = string })) so Terraform enforces the required shape directly, and simplify/remove the custom validation block accordingly (an object type already rejects missing or extra keys at plan time with a clear error).
findings.title: var.secrets is weakly typed (list(map(string))) with a custom validation that doesn't check for the specific keys the code actually requires

findings.explanation: name = "crypto-key-${random_id.random_kms_suffix.hex}s" appends a literal "s" straight onto the hex suffix with no separator (e.g. producing "crypto-key-1a2b3c4ds"), reading like a leftover typo rather than an intentional pluralization. Same pattern exists in example/examplea/google_kms_crypto_key.tf.
findings.remediation: Remove the trailing "s", or if a suffix word is intended, add a separator (e.g. "crypto-key-${random_id.random_kms_suffix.hex}-secrets").
findings.title: KMS crypto key name has a stray trailing "s" directly appended to the random suffix
